documents.title: General machine-condition response
documents.scope_notice: Generic training draft. No approved numeric limits, isolation sequence or equipment-specific operating response is provided.

Operator: Confirm the machine ID, sensor name, unit, timestamp and quality before responding.
For a Suspect condition, report the observation to your assigned supervisor and responsible maintenance team. Continue operation only if the approved site procedure permits it.
For a Critical condition, follow the equipment-specific approved safe-stop procedure. This draft does not specify a stop button, emergency-stop action or power-isolation sequence.
Keep clear of moving equipment. Do not bypass guards, open electrical panels or attempt unauthorized repair.
Record symptoms and reading references in the incident. Restart only through the approved authorization process, even if the reading returns to normal.
Supervisor: Confirm the affected machine, assigned operator and freshness of the supporting evidence.
For Suspect, prioritize the concern and assign the responsible maintenance team within your scope.
For Critical, coordinate the approved machine response and escalate to the responsible plant manager.
Coordinate workstation coverage and record the handover without disclosing unrelated machine or personnel records.
Review inspection and verification findings before accepting resolution; an app status alone does not authorize restart.
Maintenance: Review the assigned incident, exact sensor, timestamps and relevant equipment manual.
Use only the approved equipment-specific isolation and inspection procedure, performed by authorized personnel.
Inspect the reported concern using the applicable approved checklist. Do not infer a failed component solely from an unusual sensor value.
Record findings, actions and verification evidence in the assigned work order.
Follow the approved release/restart authorization. Close the incident with verification notes and confirm linked work orders are complete.
Manager: Review the affected machine/line and the reported severity with the responsible supervisor.
For Critical, confirm a response owner and coordinate the site escalation and recovery process.
Use verified production impact and investigation findings for operational decisions; the detector does not decide repair or replacement.
Track the resolution and any required authorization with the supervisor and maintenance lead.
Admin: Check ingestion health, machine identity and user/team mappings if the alert appears incorrectly routed.
Correct only authorized configuration issues and retain the audit trail.
Direct equipment operating decisions to the responsible supervisor and maintenance team; Admin access is not operating authorization.
